items.title: Quxnet.net
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
Remember when I said that I was done signing up for every new service that comes along? Yeah, me too. But...

Quxnet has everything. Boards, mail, photo galleries, links, blogs, an RSS reader, and more. It looks super-retro cool, which adds to the vibe. I don't know what I want out of it yet, but if it can remain "A private network with old internet manners." then I can see it becoming a fun new place to hang out.

There are still fewer than 1,000 people there, so naturally things are cordial and sufficiently nerdy and polite. I hope it stays polite, but I worry that with popularity comes conflicting views from people who "We" don't agree with, and once the finger-pointing starts, things tend to go south. I hope it doesn't happen that way.

But for now it's clever, fun, nerdy, and new, so I'm in. https://quxnet.net/u/jbaty.

items.title: Discord, or the Death of Lore
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I have no disputes as the popularity of [Discord], the things that happen there, and the unquestioned vivaciousness of being the party that never seems to end and everyone wants to join.

I just happen to be the sort of person who notices there’s no decent fire exits and most of the structure is wood and there’s an… awful lot of pyrotechnics being set off.

items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: I miss out on a lot by constantly going online to see what I've missed out on.

items.title: Sunday, October 18, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I was planning to stay away from computers today. I've been partially successful. I'm staring at my notebooks and thinking that I'm doing it wrong. I recently bought the gorgeous and expensive Plotter, but I don't know how it fits. Or if it fits. I wish I needed it, but I don't think I do. Great, more $$$ down the tubes on a just-in-case.

On a positive note, season 4 of The Diplomat is out and I love it. There's something about smart people doing difficult jobs as best they can.

items.title: Saturday, October 17, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I wrote software for a living for a long time. Speaking for myself, I can confidently say that Claude Code writes code that's so much better than mine that it's embarrassing. I've gotten over it. I'm not a craftsman. I wish I was, but honestly I just want to tell the computer what I need done and have it do it. I suppose that's really all I've ever wanted. Now I can, and it's thrilling.

That Tesla Roadster demo was a pretty cool stunt. Cool, but dumb. And only a stunt.

The answer to "What can [famous person]'s [something] tell us about [some other completely unrelated thing] is always, "nothing".

items.title: Curtain Fever
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: (n.): Lavishing care on the décor of a life while the life goes unattended. “She spent three weeks on the logo for a company she hasn’t started. Total curtain fever.”

items.title: What happened to the desktop metaphor?
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
The problem appears when abstraction turns into concealment.

There is way too much concealment going on.

items.title: A searchable archive of everything
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I wrote something down recently, and later I couldn't find it. If you know me, you know why; I put my notes into too many different apps.

Once in a while I declare loudly that "I'm using only this app, from now on! I mean it!" and then change my mind a month later. It's just the way I am. This most recent failure was the last straw and finally forced me to deal with it properly.

Instead of fixing myself, I built a software crutch. I spent today vibe-coding an indexer and search engine for all of my stuff. Here's the initial version of a web UI:

I also hacked together a TUI and an Emacs package. Those access the data via Tailscale SSH so I don't need to worry about installing things on other machines. Just the wrapper script.

Here's the list of sources being indexed (so far):

./archive index
baty.net: 1272 items (0.9s)
archive.baty.net: 2791 items (1.1s)
linux.baty.net: 26 items (0.0s)
blot.baty.net: 678 items (0.3s)
jackbaty.com: 581 items (0.1s)
notes: 2287 items (1.0s)
dayone: 2507 items (1.4s)
thebrain: 1177 items (0.5s)
mail: 1 updated, 0 removed (since revision 43773) (1.6s)
duplicates: 786 items in 381 groups (10.2s)

One nice thing about this is now I can search all of my Denote notes from my phone.

Everything is plain files and it uses boring, durable tools, so the archive should outlive whichever apps made the content that week. Even an AI layer, if I add one, sits on top of the search instead of being built into it. The database is disposable because it only takes 10 seconds to reindex everything.

Maybe now I'll be OK with all of my app churn.

items.title: Thursday, October 15, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I swear if I hear the word "slop" one more time I'm going to punch someone in the throat.

I just did a nice and thorough de-cluttering of my office and I feel much better.

I'm tightening my requirements for people I follow. Their contribute-to-complain ratio needs to tend toward ∞.

I've started eating meals sitting at my kitchen table with no devices nearby. Sometimes I'll have a book open, but otherwise it's just me and the world. Food tastes better this way.

Have you notices that most of the entries on these daily notes start with "I..."? It bugs me sometimes, but then again, it's my blog and these are my daily notes, so
